WHY THE PIN IS EXACT, AND WHY A VK CHECK WILL NOT PROTECT YOU. Measured, both directions, with
the same-toolchain control run first:
- withdraw_identity's recursion VK is BYTE-IDENTICAL under 5.1.0 and 6.0. Same 115 fields,
same values. A pinned-VK check - which is exactly what inner_vk.nr is - sees nothing wrong.
- Its proofs are mutually unverifiable anyway. Each verifies against its own bb; each fails
against the other at `UltraVerifier: verification failed at reduction step`.
- The emitted Solidity moved 2,491 -> 2,518 lines, 99 lines differing, with ZERO VK constants
changed. So the TEMPLATE is what breaks a verifier, and the key cannot tell you.
